9470-his-hour.title: His Hour
9470-his-hour.creator: Elinor Glyn
9470-his-hour.description: A book by Elinor Glyn. And if you have one, what have you done with it hitherto? Are you any light in the world?--No, you have lived upon the orders of others, you have let your individuality be crushed these twenty-four years--since the day you could speak. Just an echo it is--that fine thing, your soul! Show it then, if you have one!

arxiv-2103-05311.title: Energy-Efficient MAC for Cellular IoT: State-of-the-Art, Challenges, and Standardization
arxiv-2103-05311.creator: Syed Waqas Haider Shah, Student Member, IEEE , Adnan Noor Mian, Member, IEEE , Adnan Aijaz, Senior Member, IEEE , Junaid Qadir, Senior Member, IEEE , and Jon Crowcroft, Fellow, IEEE
arxiv-2103-05311.description: Abstract In the modern world, the connectivity-as-we-go model is gaining popularity. Internet-of-Things (IoT) envisions a future in which human beings communicate with each other and with devices that have identities and virtual personalities, as well as sensing, processing, and networking capabilities, which will allow the developing of smart environments that operate with little or no human intervention.

arxiv-2202-00938.title: Fourier characterizations and non-triviality of Gelfand-Shilov spaces, with applications to Toeplitz operators
arxiv-2202-00938.creator: Albin Petersson
arxiv-2202-00938.description: Abstract . We examine properties of Gelfand-Shilov spaces S s S_{s} , S σ S^{\sigma} , S s σ S_{s}^{\sigma} , Σ s \Sigma_{s} , Σ σ \Sigma^{\sigma} and Σ s σ \Sigma_{s}^{\sigma} . These are spaces of smooth functions where the functions or their Fourier transforms admit sub-exponential decay.

arxiv-2203-09653.title: Regional Semantic Contrast and Aggregation for Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation
arxiv-2203-09653.creator: Tianfei Zhou, Meijie Zhang, Fang Zhao, Jianwu Li
arxiv-2203-09653.description: Abstract Learning semantic segmentation from weakly-labeled ( e.g . , image tags only) data is challenging since it is hard to infer dense object regions from sparse semantic tags. Despite being broadly studied, most current efforts directly learn from limited semantic annotations carried by individual image or image pairs, and struggle to obtain integral localization maps.

arxiv-2304-13164.title: Towards Compute-Optimal Transfer Learning
arxiv-2304-13164.creator: Massimo Caccia, Alexandre Galashov, Arthur Douillard, Amal Rannen-Triki, Dushyant Rao, Michela Paganini, Laurent Charlin, Marc’aurelio Ranzato, Razvan Pascanu
arxiv-2304-13164.description: Abstract The field of transfer learning is undergoing a significant shift with the introduction of large pretrained models which have demonstrated strong adaptability to a variety of downstream tasks. However, the high computational and memory requirements to finetune or use these models can be a hindrance to their widespread use.

arxiv-2401-11296.title: Induced Turán problem in bipartite graphs
arxiv-2401-11296.creator: Maria Axenovich, Jakob Zimmermann
arxiv-2401-11296.description: Abstract The classical extremal function for a graph H H , ex ⁡ ( K n , H ) {\rm ex}(K_{n},H) is the largest number of edges in a subgraph of K n K_{n} that contains no subgraph isomorphic to H H .

arxiv-2402-15211.title: Primordial black holes as a dark matter candidate - a brief overview Journal: Nuclear Physics B
arxiv-2402-15211.creator: Anne M. Green
arxiv-2402-15211.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Anne M. Green. Historically the most popular dark matter candidates have been new elementary particles, such as Weakly Interacting Massive Particles and axions. However Primordial Black Holes (PBHs), black holes formed from overdensities in the early Universe, are another possibility. The discovery of gravitational waves from mergers of tens of Solar mass black hole binaries by LIGO-Virgo has generated a surge in interest in PBH dark matter.

arxiv-2405-03251.title: Exploring the Frontiers of Softmax: Provable Optimization, Applications in Diffusion Model, and Beyond
arxiv-2405-03251.creator: Yang Cao and Yingyu Liang and Zhenmei Shi and Zhao Song
arxiv-2405-03251.description: Abstract The softmax activation function plays a crucial role in the success of large language models (LLMs), particularly in the self-attention mechanism of the widely adopted Transformer architecture. However, the underlying learning dynamics that contribute to the effectiveness of softmax remain largely unexplored.

arxiv-2406-09580.title: Steady-state work extraction from two coupled qubits embedded within equilibrium and non-equilibrium reservoirs
arxiv-2406-09580.creator: Maryam Hadipour, Soroush Haseli
arxiv-2406-09580.description: Abstract Work extraction is a fundamental aspect in thermodynamics. In the context of quantum physics, ergotropy quantifies the maximum amount of work that can be obtained from quantum system through cyclic unitary process. In this work, the steady-state ergotropy of two coupled qubit, each interacting locally with its individual boson or fermion reservoir, will be examined.

arxiv-2410-20768.title: Task Confusion and Catastrophic Forgetting in Class-Incremental Learning: A Mathematical Framework for Discriminative and Generative Modelings
arxiv-2410-20768.creator: Milad Khademi Nori, Il-Min Kim
arxiv-2410-20768.description: Abstract In class-incremental learning (class-IL), models must classify all previously seen classes at test time without task-IDs, leading to task confusion. Despite being a key challenge, task confusion lacks a theoretical understanding. We present a novel mathematical framework for class-IL and prove the Infeasibility Theorem, showing optimal class-IL is impossible with discriminative modeling due to task confusion.

arxiv-2412-03259.title: GERD: Geometric event response data generation Thanks: EC Horizon 2020 Framework Programme under Grant Agreements 785907 and 945539 (J.E.P., D.K., J.C.), the Pioneer Centre for AI, under the Danish National Research Foundation grant number P1 (J.E.P, D.K).
arxiv-2412-03259.creator: Jens Egholm Pedersen, Dimitris Korakovounis, Jörg Conradt
arxiv-2412-03259.description: Abstract Event-based vision sensors are appealing because of their time resolution, higher dynamic range, and low-power consumption. They also provide data that is fundamentally different from conventional frame-based cameras: events are sparse, discrete, and require integration in time. Unlike conventional models grounded in established geometric and physical principles, event-based models lack comparable foundations.

arxiv-2506-05088.title: Semi-Implicit Variational Inference via Kernelized Path Gradient Descent
arxiv-2506-05088.creator: Tobias Pielok, Bernd Bischl, David Rügamer
arxiv-2506-05088.description: Abstract Semi-implicit variational inference (SIVI) is a powerful framework for approximating complex posterior distributions, but training with the Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence can be challenging due to high variance and bias in high-dimensional settings. While current state-of-the-art semi-implicit variational inference methods, particularly Kernel Semi-Implicit Variational Inference (KSIVI), have been shown to work in high dimensions, training remains moderately expensive.

arxiv-2601-18774.title: The Blown Lead Paradox: Conditional Laws for the Running Maximum of Binary Doob Martingales
arxiv-2601-18774.creator: Jonathan Pipping-Gamón & Abraham J. Wyner Department of Statistics, University of Pennsylvania
arxiv-2601-18774.description: Abstract Live win-probability forecasts are now ubiquitous in sports broadcasts, and retrospective commentary often cites the largest win probability attained by a team that ultimately loses as evidence of a “collapse.” Interpreting such extrema requires a reference distribution under correct specification.

plos-pone-0006240.creator: Thomas Michelet, Bernard Bioulac, Dominique Guehl et al.
plos-pone-0006240.description: PLOS ONE research article. Learning from mistakes is a key feature of human behavior. However, the mechanisms underlying short-term adaptation to erroneous action are still poorly understood. One possibility relies on the modulation of attentional systems after an error. To explore this possibility, we hav

pmc-10621159.title: Sex-related differences for uric acid in the prediction of cardiovascular events in essential hypertension. A population prospective study
pmc-10621159.creator: Maria Perticone, Raffaele Maio, Ermal Shehaj, Simona Gigliotti, Benedetto Caroleo, Edoardo Suraci, Angela Sciacqua, Francesco Andreozzi, Francesco Perticone
pmc-10621159.description: BackgroundUric acid (UA) is an independent prognostic factor for cardiovascular events, but there are no data demonstrating a different risk profile between women and men. Thus, we tested whether UA is associated with a possible sex-related difference in fatal and non-fatal cardiovascular events.MethodsIn this prospective population-based study we enrolled 1,650 never-treated Caucasian hypertensive outpatients referred to Catanzaro University Hospital (Italy).

pmc-10717324.title: Media matters: culture medium-dependent hypervariable phenotype of mesenchymal stromal cells
pmc-10717324.creator: Joan C. Fitzgerald, Georgina Shaw, J. Mary Murphy, Frank Barry
pmc-10717324.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundDespite a long history of investigation and sustained efforts in clinical testing, the number of market authorisations for mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) therapies remains limited, with none approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration. Several barriers are impeding the clinical progression of MSC therapies, to the forefront of these is a lack of standardised manufacturing protocols which is further compounded by an absence of biologically meaningful characterisation and release assays.

pmc-11046670.title: Interventions to promote medication adherence for chronic diseases in India: a systematic review
pmc-11046670.creator: Abraham Tolley, Refaat Hassan, Kirpal Grewal, Ruige Kong, Rohan Sanghera, Baani Sodhi, Saurav Basu
pmc-11046670.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). dia.2, 3 Low adherence is associated with poor patient outcomes that further accentuates healthcare costs.4 Implementing cost-effective interventions targeted at improving adherence are urgently warranted to improve outcomes and reduce complications arising from the growing burden of chronic diseases. However, the majority of evidence for medication adherence improving strategies is based on more economically developed countries and existing reviews in low- and middle-income countries tend to focus on specific diseases across countries.

pmc-11298543.title: Insights into immune microenvironment and therapeutic targeting in androgen-associated prostate cancer subtypes
pmc-11298543.creator: Liang Huang, Yu Xie, Shusuan Jiang, Tao Dai, Zhenzhou Xu, Hong Shan
pmc-11298543.description: Prostate cancer, one of the most prevalent malignancies among men worldwide, is intricately linked with androgen signaling, a key driver of its pathogenesis and progression. Understanding the diverse expression patterns of androgen-responsive genes holds paramount importance in unraveling the biological intricacies of this disease and prognosticating patient outcomes.

pmc-11354427.title: Exploring Biodiversity through the Lens of Knautia arvensis Pollinators: Knautia Pollinator Walks as a Monitoring Method
pmc-11354427.creator: Markus Franzén, Magnus Stenmark
pmc-11354427.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryMonitoring pollinator populations is crucial for understanding biodiversity trends and ensuring the health of ecosystems, especially in agricultural landscapes. This study introduces the “Knautia Pollinator Walk” as a new method for tracking pollinator diversity and abundance. By observing pollinators visiting the inflorescence of Knautia arvensis, we found significant correlations between pollinators and land use, and there were significant differences in pollinator communities between regions.

pmc-11592805.title: CURATE: Scaling-Up Differentially Private Causal Graph Discovery
pmc-11592805.creator: Payel Bhattacharjee, Ravi Tandon, Dawn E Holmes
pmc-11592805.description: Causal graph discovery (CGD) is the process of estimating the underlying probabilistic graphical model that represents the joint distribution of features of a dataset. CGD algorithms are broadly classified into two categories: (i) constraint-based algorithms, where the outcome depends on conditional independence (CI) tests, and (ii) score-based algorithms, where the outcome depends on optimized score function.

pmc-11596180.title: An Automated Digital Microfluidic System Based on Inkjet Printing
pmc-11596180.creator: Wansheng Hu, Ming Cao, Lingni Liao, Yuanhong Liao, Yuhan He, Mengxiao Ma, Simao Wang, Yimin Guan
pmc-11596180.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Cellular interactions, such as intercellular communication and signal transduction, can be enhanced within three-dimensional cell spheroids, contributing significantly to cellular viability and proliferation. This is crucial for advancements in cancer research, drug testing, and personalized medicine. The dimensions of the cell spheroids play a pivotal role in their functionality, affecting cell proliferation and differentiation, intercellular interactions, gene expression, protein synthesis, drug penetration, and metabolism. Consequently, different spheroid sizes may be required for various drug sensitivity experiments.

pmc-11730182.title: Achieving room air quality of room class Ib in the aseptic area using a mobile sterile ventilation unit in a room class II surgical unit
pmc-11730182.creator: Dorothee Boppre, Martin Exner, Colin M. Krüger, Hannes Schuler, Michael Wendt, Julian-Camill Harnoss, Axel Kramer
pmc-11730182.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Introduction: Room air class (RC) Ib may be necessary for surgical procedures in aseptic working areas. The aim of the study was to examine whether a mobile, three-stage sterile ventilation unit (MSVU) can replace a room ventilation system (RVS) with turbulent mixed flow (TMF) in the area of the operating field and on the instrument table from hygienic-microbiological point of view.

pmc-12525264.title: The Biological Role and Clinical Significance of BECLIN-1 in Cancer
pmc-12525264.creator: Chinmay Maheshwari, Andrea Castiglioni, Uthman Walusimbi, Chiara Vidoni, Alessandra Ferraresi, Danny N Dhanasekaran, Ciro Isidoro, Nam Deuk Kim
pmc-12525264.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BECLIN-1 is a multidomain protein that, through dynamic interaction with a variety of partners, controls autophagy and apoptosis, two processes dysregulated in cancer cells, thus playing a crucial role in cell fate. Although mutations in the BECN1 gene are rare in cancer, its frequent monoallelic deletion contributes to spontaneous cancer initiation by impairing autophagy, establishing it as a haploinsufficient tumor suppressor gene. The expression and activity of BECLIN-1 are further modulated by epigenetic mechanisms, alternative splicing, post-translational modifications, and alternative partner interactions.

pmc-12722050.title: Aotearoa New Zealand pet guardians’ attitudes towards the financial cost of pet care
pmc-12722050.creator: Leena Awawdeh, Natalie Waran, Rachel H Forrest
pmc-12722050.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Pet guardianship is a common practice globally that enhances human well-being by offering companionship and emotional support. However, it also entails financial responsibilities that can pose challenges to both human and animal well-being. This study used an online survey distributed between January and March 2019 to adults residing in Aotearoa New Zealand (NZ), to investigate financial aspects of pet guardianship, including the importance of pet insurance, the impact of veterinary costs, and the ethical considerations of owning a pet.

pmc-13037045.title: External validation of risk indices and the development of a multivariable risk prediction model for surgical site infection in adults: a prospective observational study
pmc-13037045.creator: Darren P. R. Troeman, Stephan Harbarth, Jan A. J. W. Kluytmans, C. H. van Werkhoven
pmc-13037045.description: BackgroundTo enable proper benchmarking of rates of surgical site infections (SSIs), it is important to consider the variability in case mix and risk factors in the data analysis. SSI risk indices have been used to make the data more comparable. However, different risk indices exist, and studies comparing these indices head-to-head are limited.

pmc-13099085.title: Workplace Injuries and Return-to-Work Challenges Among Immigrants in Canada: Implications for Occupational Health Policy and Practice
pmc-13099085.creator: Shu-Ping Chen, Janki Shankar, Tanvir C Turin, Shawn Joseph, Rhea Narayanan, Zabin Suleman, Benedicta Asante, Priyadarshini Kharat
pmc-13099085.description: This study examined the experiences of immigrant workers in Alberta, Canada, following work-related injuries, with a focus on postinjury reporting and return-to-work challenges. Twenty-seven injured immigrant employees from various industries were interviewed. Using an interpretive analysis approach, the study identified key factors shaping their experiences. Most participants were educationally overqualified for their roles and unfamiliar with high-risk, labor-intensive work environments.

pmc-13179264.title: Evaluation of sNfL as a Biomarker for Paclitaxel-Induced Peripheral Neurotoxicity Through an Integrated PKPD Model
pmc-13179264.creator: Eman I K Ibrahim, Milda Girdenyté, Yang Hu, Lorenzo Di Cesare Mannelli, David Balayssac, Jérôme Busserolles, Diethilde Theil, Gautier Roussignol, Olivier Perrault, Nathalie Le Berre, Franck Chanut, Mohamed Slaoui, Irena Loryan, Lena E Friberg
pmc-13179264.description: BackgroundSerum neurofilament light chain (sNfL), a biomarker of axonal damage, has shown promise in clinical studies for monitoring paclitaxel-induced peripheral neurotoxicity (PIPN). The latter involves pathological changes in PIPN sites such as the dorsal root ganglia, peripheral nerves, and brain. However, the mechanistic link between paclitaxel and NfL concentrations in these tissues remains poorly understood, necessitating preclinical investigation.

pmc-13357536.title: Deep learning single-cell analysis for cytologic evaluation of oral potentially malignant disorders
pmc-13357536.creator: Michael P McRae, Kritika S Rajsri, Nadarajah Vigneswaran, A Ross Kerr, Spencer W Redding, Martin H Thornhill, Craig Murdoch, Paul M Speight, Nancy Ruel, Rachelle Wolk, Ryan R Ruff, John T McDevitt
pmc-13357536.description: Oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs) such as leukoplakia and erythroplakia may harbor dysplasia or progress to oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), yet visual inspection alone is unreliable for risk assessment. Cytology offers a minimally invasive adjunct, but conventional approaches depend on manual feature extraction and subjective review.

pmc-13364220.title: DASH, Mediterranean, and Plant-Based Diets and Cancer Risk in Women: A Narrative Review Based on Diet Quality Indices
pmc-13364220.creator: Iwona Lasek, Magdalena Makarewicz-Wujec
pmc-13364220.description: Cancer remains a major public health challenge among women worldwide, and diet quality may play an important role in cancer prevention. This narrative review synthesized evidence on the association between standardized diet quality indices—the DASH Score, Mediterranean Diet Score, and plant-based diet indices—and the risk of selected cancers in women, focusing on breast, colorectal, and ovarian cancer.

pmc-13370867.creator: Romana Ďuráčiová, Michaela Capandová, Karel Berka, Radka Svobodová, Terézia Slanináková, Kristián Kováč, Matej Antol, Lukáš Hejtmánek

pmc-13396441.creator: János Rokai, Melinda Rácz, Melinda Becske, János Csipor, Csaba Márton Köllőd, István Ulbert, Gergely Márton

pmc-13401934.title: Deciphering the Multi-Target Therapeutic Mechanisms of Traditional Chinese Medicine Against Alzheimer’s Disease: A Network Pharmacology Perspective
pmc-13401934.creator: Yiyi Zhang, Gaofeng Qin, Qinaqian Lian, Yuanyuan Sun, Zhe Liu, Bing Chen, Zhenhua Li, Na Li, Rongqiang Song, Yujiu Wang
pmc-13401934.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) poses a growing threat to global health, with no disease-modifying therapies currently available to cure or reverse its progression. Given its favorable safety profile and multi-target nature, Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) has attracted increasing attention as a potential strategy for AD prevention and treatment.
